title: Finite projective summands inherit Tor independence
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and let A and B be commutative R-algebras. For R-modules M,N, write Tor_i^R(M,N) for the i-th homology module of a projective-resolution tensor complex (i.e. the usual Tor groups [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]). Assume Tor_i^R(A,B)=0 for every i>0. If P is an A-module that is a direct summand of A^m for some finite m (a finite projective A-module), then Tor_i^R(P,B)=0 for every i>0.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: For each i>0, compute Tor_i^R(A^m,B) using the finite direct sum of m copies of a projective resolution of A. Tensoring this resolution with B and taking homology commute with finite direct sums, so Tor_i^R(A^m,B) is the direct sum of m copies of Tor_i^R(A,B), hence is zero by the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: Choose $A$-linear maps $s\colon P\to A^m$ and $r\colon A^m\to P$ with $r\circ s=\mathrm{id}_P$. Functoriality of $\operatorname{Tor}$ in its first module [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] carries these to maps $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(P,B)\to\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(A^m,B)\to\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(P,B)$ whose composite is the identity. Thus $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(P,B)$ is a direct summand of the zero module $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(A^m,B)$ (Step 1), and is therefore zero for every $i>0$.
